previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, bilateral lower extremity amputations, and a complex history of recurrent infections was admitted for nausea, dyspnea, and hypertension. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and a positive urine analysis, prompting broad-spectrum antibiotics. Stool testing confirmed Clostridium difficile infection, leading to discontinuation of IV cefepime and initiation of oral vancomycin. Her Foley catheter was changed due to concern for contamination. She responded well to treatment, with resolution of nausea and stabilization of vital signs. Her diabetes management was adjusted after two episodes of hypoglycemia, and her heart failure and hypertension were managed with continued carvedilol and dialysis. She completed a dialysis session during admission and was discharged home on a two-week course of oral vancomycin with follow-up arranged.
